identity.title: ALMA Observations of the Largest Proto-Planetary Disk in the Orion Nebula, 114-426: A CO Silhouette

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA observations of the largest protoplanetary disk in the Orion Nebula, 114-426.

evidence.quote: With a major axis diameter of 2.3$''$ , or 950 AU at a distance of 414 pc (cite: Menten2007), the 114-426 disk is the largest silhouette in the Orion Nebula

question.value: What are the dust mass, gas tracers and CO kinematics (central star mass) of the largest silhouette disk in the Orion Nebula, 114-426, from ALMA Band 7 data?

evidence.quote: we present the ALMA observations of the 114-426 disk in four spectral lines and re-analyze the dust continuum in more detail than (cite: Mann2014).
obtained with ALMA during Cycle 0 (ALMA project 2011.0.00028.S) on 24 October 2012
Four transitions were observed in ALMA Band 7; CO J=3$-$2, HCO$^+$ J=4$-$3, HCN J=4$-$3, and CS J=7$-$6.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive disk mass from dust continuum

method.value: Optically thin M = S D^2/(kappa B(T))

evidence.quote: $$M_{disk}  = {{S_{\nu} D^2} \over {\kappa B_{\nu}(T_{dust}) }}

assumptions.value: kappa=0.034 cm^2/g, gas-to-dust 100, T_dust=20 K, D=414 pc

evidence.quote: a grain emissivity $\kappa$ = 0.034 ${\rm cm}^2~{\rm g}^{-1}$ (which assumes a gas-to-dust ratio of 100), and a grain temperature $T_{dust}$ = 20 K

analysis_steps.goal: Measure CO absorption depths and velocities

method.value: Locate deepest absorption per channel; convert Jy/beam to K; compare with interpolated single-dish background

evidence.quote: Table 2 lists the location of the deepest absorption as a function of radial velocity, the absorption depth in Janskys and degrees Kelvin

validation.value: Cube rms of ~0.1 Jy in background is smaller than absorption signal

evidence.quote: the CO intensity fluctuations in the ALMA data cube have a 1 $\sigma$ rms of about 0.1 Jy or less

method.value: Keplerian from separation and velocity difference of absorption minima; plus thin optically thick Keplerian disk model convolved with beam

evidence.quote: We modeled the CO absorption from a geometrically thin, optically thick Keplerian disk inclined by a few degrees, convolved with a Gaussian to represent the synthesized ALMA beam

findings_qualitative.value: Disk is not detected in HCO+, HCN or CS.

evidence.quote: HCO$^+$, HCN, and CS lines, in either emission or absorption, are not detected from 114-426.

claims.hypothesis: Does the 114-426 disk have a low mass?
claims.finding: Low mass disk, possibly a lower limit if grains are large

evidence.quote: the observed sub-mm dust continuum implies a disk mass of 3.1$\pm$0.6 times the mass of Jupiter

claims.hypothesis: Can the central star mass be constrained from CO absorption?
claims.experiment: Keplerian analysis of absorption minima plus model
claims.result: M* ~0.43 Msun; 0.4-0.7 favored for small hole

evidence.quote: indicates that $M_*$ is less than 1 M$_{\odot}$ with a most likely value around 0.4 M$_{\odot}$.

claims.hypothesis: Is the disk evolved/depleted in dense gas tracers?
claims.finding: May indicate evolved disk, but only suggestive

evidence.quote: Thus, the absence of measurable HCN, CS, and HCO$^+$ lines may also be an indication that the 114-426 disk is highly evolved.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Large (~250 AU) inner hole with ~1 Msun star also allowed by model

evidence.quote: A stellar mass of about 1 M$_{\odot}$ and a thin annular disk with a large ($\sim$ 250 AU) hole, however, is also allowed.

limitations_admitted.value: Mass is a lower limit if solids are in large grains

evidence.quote: If most solids and ices have have been incorporated into large grains, however, this value is a lower limit.

limitations_admitted.value: Beam dilution and background brightness limit CO absorption interpretation

evidence.quote: The observed CO absorption can be affected by several factors including the optical depth, radial velocity, and temperature of the disk gas, beam dilution

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-dish background interpolated from other transitions, not measured in CO 3-2
Star mass from only two absorption minima; rough Keplerian assumption
Model fit is poorly documented; no uncertainties on model
Fixed T=20 K and kappa dominate mass uncertainty
